author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.57.1. Docstring and the 'Fallback only - the installed distribution's metadata is authoritative' comment are both still exact; the literal moved 0.57.0 -> 0.57.1, which is the only reason this staled. The stale-bytecode condition this literal keeps triggering remains memway-tasks#13, unfixed by choice.

WORTH KNOWING, learned by getting it wrong in this release's own ceremony: verify-change computes staled_knowledge against the SAVED INDEX, so an edit that lands after verify-change and before index is invisible to the gate. The version bump here landed in that window; verify-change printed 0 staled, index re-stamped the entity, and this note stayed silently stale until viz's repo-wide count disagreed. The ceremony order (verify-change, then index) is not a style preference - anything edited after that first call is unchecked, and this coordinate is the one guaranteed to be edited every single release.

author: agent
text:
Re-read at 0.57.2, and this should be the LAST entry of its kind on this coordinate.

The seven confirms below are all the same confirm. Each says the docstring and the "Fallback only" comment are still accurate, and each exists because the version literal moved, which moved this module's logic hash, which staled everything attached to it. Seven releases answered a question the tool already knew the answer to, and each answer cost a paragraph. memway-tasks#13 was open across all seven, marked "unfixed by choice".

0.57.2 removes the literal. __version__ is now derived by _derive_version(): pyproject.toml when this package sits in a source tree or editable install, distribution metadata otherwise, with the pyproject only believed if it declares name = "memway". So the file no longer changes at release, and this coordinate should not stale on a bump again. It staled THIS time legitimately - the module gained a function.

The second thing that closes: the stale-.pyc flake, at the root rather than in the test. There is no version compiled into this module's bytecode, so cache staleness cannot produce version staleness - old bytecode still runs a function that reads today's pyproject. 0.55.5 fixed the test by reading both files as text, which was right and left the cause standing.

Comments verified: the module docstring is exact, and _derive_version's docstring describes what the body does, including the ordering rule (source tree wins for an editable checkout; metadata wins for a wheel, which has no pyproject beside it) and why - cli._version still owns the editable-vs-wheel decision, this only defines what "the source says" means.

If this coordinate stales on a future release WITHOUT this file changing, that is a real signal and not the old ritual - check what started writing to it.
